W4 CONFLUENCE GRAPH v1 — CONCRETE DESIGN RECOMMENDATION

CONSTITUTION: display-only under Article 2 (§68 NEURAL_WEB_MASTERPLAN_BY_FABLE.md). No confluence state may RAISE a ranking, ordering, or alert priority until it holds SHADOW-with-track-record tier. No cross-engine hard gate without its own gauntlet (China falsification law). Oracle artifacts consumed READ-ONLY.

--- NODE VOCABULARY ---

Six node types, all already present in the bus:

1. ENGINE nodes — one per bus family today: us_board, altdata, radar, policy, desk:ai_desk, track_record (spine_index engine column values). Key: engine name.

2. SECTOR/BASKET nodes — from oracle_state.json complexes[] (8 complexes) + synapse.yml's sector_pulse artifacts (11 GICS sectors). Key: complex id or basket slug.

3. TICKER/ENTITY nodes — symbols present in spine_index.parquet (entity scope_type rows). For W4 v1 keep to top-N by signal density to stay readable.

4. REGIME nodes — 4 regime buckets from kernel_estimates.parquet: Goldilocks, Reflation, Stagflation, Recession + the __all__ marginal. Key: quad_hard_label value.

5. THESIS nodes — active radar theses from data/radar/theses.jsonl (8 consumers including qledger). Key: thesis id.

6. EPISODE nodes — active episodes from oracle_state.json active_episodes[] (173 today). Key: node+direction+onset_date.

--- EDGE VOCABULARY ---

Four edge types, with the ones MEASURABLE TODAY from existing artifacts marked:

A. "feeds" edges — structural data-flow, always valid, from synapse.yml producer→consumer graph.
   MEASURABLE TODAY: all 94 synapse artifacts have a listed producer + consumer list. Extract as directed edges (producer_module → artifact → consumer_module). This is the "infrastructure" layer of the graph — not a learned relationship, but the wiring facts.

B. "confirms" edges — two engines agree on the same ticker/direction on the same date.
   MEASURABLE TODAY (partial): briefing.py's n_facets + source_mix per ticker (L89-90) already counts how many facets agree. For a date-level co-firing lift, join spine_index rows with the same (symbol, as_of, direction, horizon) across different engine values → compute mean(outcome_excess | both_fire) − mean(outcome_excess | either_fire). This is the "co-firing lift" the masterplan references. The spine_index parquet has the raw data (engine, symbol, as_of, direction, outcome_excess, quad_hard_label). The computation is a grouped join — implementable in ~20 lines of pandas. HOWEVER: spine_index today has ~651 rows (529 us_board, 120 altdata_conv, 2 desk); co-firing cells across engine pairs will be thin (n<10 in most pairs). Ship as a display table with n printed per cell, never asserting lift without MIN_N_ROUTING=10 floor. NOT a gauntlet result — label as estimate.

C. "leads" edges — Oracle-native, from data/oracle/graph_m.json["leadlag"]. Currently 56 complex-pair records, n_is_leader=0 at complex level (no lag>0 dominates lag=0 at current panel depth). The edge-stability ledger (18745 stable pairs in Tier-M) IS the "structurally co-moves" relationship — not a lead, but the "confirms in RS-change space" relationship. MEASURABLE TODAY: read graph_m.json and graph_s.json edge_stability records directly. For W4 v1, present stable=True pairs as "structurally linked" display annotations on the sector/basket nodes.

D. "contradicts" edges — generalizes briefing.py divergences block. Two engines have opposite directional reads on the same ticker/date: news_dir × supply_dir < 0 (briefing.py:101). The cross_asset_confirm snapshot() "diverge" verdict (engine/cross_asset_confirm.py:374) is a macro-level contradicts edge (bonds+FX vs equity). MEASURABLE TODAY: scan intelligence by_ticker bundle for divergent labels; scan cross_asset_confirm output for verdict="diverge". Both are already computed nightly.

The following must NOT be in the W4 v1 artifact as anything other than display estimates with n printed:
- Engine co-firing lift (confirms edges from spine): thin sample (n<10 in most pairs). Can compute and display with explicit "n=X, pre-gauntlet estimate" label.
- Leadlag "leads" edges from Oracle: is_leader=False for all complex pairs today. Display the best_lag and best_corr numbers but do not label any pair "A leads B" without gauntlet.

1. feeds edges (30 min): parse synapse.yml, emit producer→artifact→consumer directed graph. Already exists as the SIGNAL_BUS.md Mermaid diagram; extract to JSON.
2. contradicts display (1h): join briefing.py divergences output + cross_asset_confirm verdict into the graph's edge list. Both are already nightly artifacts.

5. routing display edges (30 min): the 6 display-with-edge routing cells from p3b_routing_placebo.json. These are the only Oracle-derived directional edges with gauntlet backing (display-grade).
6. kernel regime annotations on engine nodes (1h): read kernel_estimates.parquet, attach shrunken_ic per engine per regime as a node annotation (not an edge) — "altdata engine in Goldilocks: shrunken_ic=X (n=Y, display-estimate)."

reflex.whitehouse_pattern:
WHITEHOUSE SINGLE-WRITER JSONL PATTERN (the append-race law precedent)

PATHS:
- data/whitehouse/processed.json — dedup state dict; schema {"seen": {guid: {id, at, activated, importance}}}; read/written by SOLE writer: scripts/build_whitehouse.py:build() via engine/whitehouse_feed.py:load_processed/save_processed; structure: single JSON file overwritten atomically (not append)
- data/whitehouse/alerts.jsonl — activated-alert ledger; append-only; one JSON object per line; SOLE writer: scripts/build_whitehouse.py:_append_ledger() (via `open(p, "a")`) — the whitehouse-sentinel.yml workflow; the daily build passes page_only=True which explicitly skips all ledger/state writes
- data/whitehouse/health.json — run-status dict (posts_seen, evaluated, activated, provider, as_of, gate_scores); overwritten each run; format: {"schema":"wh_health.v1", "as_of":..., "posts_seen":..., ...}
- data/whitehouse/reply_cache/<sha256>.txt — per-prompt content-hash cache (temperature=0 determinism contract); one file per (model, system, user) hash; prevents re-billing on idempotent re-evals
- site/wh_banner.json — live banners (non-expired); rebuilt idempotently from the ledger; written only when content changes (no heartbeat spam); format: {"schema":"wh_banner.v1","alerts":[...]}
- site/whitehouse.html — report page; rebuilt idempotently; written only on change
- site/whdata/<id>.json — per-alert deep-link payload; one file per activated alert

THE APPEND-RACE LAW (single-writer contract):
1. ONLY whitehouse-sentinel.yml is the writer of alerts.jsonl + processed.json. The daily build calls build(page_only=True) which explicitly short-circuits all feed/brain/ledger/state writes and only re-renders the banner JSON + HTML from the already-committed ledger (scripts/build_whitehouse.py:build(), page_only guard at line ~174). This prevents the two workflows from racing to double-spend: "so the two workflows can never race to append-then-`-X theirs`-clobber an alert or revert the dedupe state."
2. The sentinel's commit step stages ONLY its known outputs: `git add data/whitehouse data/qledger site/wh_banner.json site/whitehouse.html site/whdata` — it never touches files owned by other pipelines.
3. Dedup by guid happens in two layers: (a) in-memory during collect() (seen set collapses the 3-feed overlap), (b) processed.json keyed on guid prevents re-evaluating already-seen items across runs. On --reeval mode, the processed.json check is skipped but the reply_cache still prevents re-billing on identical prompt hashes.
4. No commit on quiet runs (idempotent artifacts): _write_if_changed() compares new text to existing file before writing; a quiet hour leaves processed.json updated (eval timestamps) but if wh_banner.json + whitehouse.html are unchanged, git diff --cached is empty → no commit → no spurious Pages deploy.
5. qledger adapter (W5): _register_wh_claim() appends to data/qledger/claims.jsonl via qledger.register() (open "a") for each activated alert's tickers — this JSONL is also single-writer per the nightly collect pipeline; the sentinel stages it explicitly so the claim ships with the alert commit.

HOW NIGHTLY FOLDS IT:
- grade_qledger.py:run() (called as end-of-collect hook) reads data/qledger/claims.jsonl, grades all claims at 5/21/63d horizons where sufficient trading days have elapsed and price data exists, writes data/qledger/grades.jsonl + site/qledger/track_record.json. The whitehouse claim_family is registered in config/qual_ladder.yml (whitehouse.alert entry, ladder_state: SHADOW) so it participates in the nightly grader automatically.
- The grader is idempotent: (claim_id, horizon_d) pairs that already have a grade row are never double-graded (scripts/grade_qledger.py:run(), n_already_graded tracking).
- Processed.json dedup is the upstream gate: if a guid was already evaluated, new_items() filters it out so the brain never re-fires and no duplicate claim is registered. The reply_cache is the cost guard for the --reeval path.

KEY DESIGN LAW EXTENDED TO REFLEXES (from masterplan §N6): "each reflex appends to its own single-writer JSONL stream (data/reflexes/<name>/firings.jsonl, the whitehouse pattern); the NIGHTLY grader folds firings into the spine — no intraday writer ever touches spine parquet." This means reflexes get their own per-name JSONL (not a shared one), the nightly grader picks them up the same way it picks up qledger claims (by claim_family), and the firings.jsonl is graded exactly like any other claim in claims.jsonl.

On each call: load last N hours of sends, filter out any alert whose (source, type, asset) key appears there, dispatch remaining, append new sends with sent_at timestamp.

The push payload per alert:
  "{source_icon} {headline}\n{detail}\n  conviction: {action} | priority: {score}/100\n  → {site_url}/{link}"

PRIORITY FLOORS (per Article-2 mandate — only act-tier or clearly critical alerts get push):
  - HARD floor: priority >= 60 (= act tier 40 + critical severity 30 + any recency − 10 buffer). This admits only act/critical or act/major-fresh alerts. No context-tier alert can exceed 48 even if fresh + confirmed; those stay display-only.
  - SOFT override: any alert with tier="act" and band="critical" regardless of score (to catch age-penalized legacy act alerts whose score dropped below 60 but still carry cross-asset act conviction).
  - EXPLICIT FLOOR EXCEPTIONS (alerts that may never push regardless of score, per Article-2): rotation entered_book/left_book/leadership_rotation (documented-null IC, capped to minor — already enforced by ic_severity_cap but add explicit push-suppress flag). altdata convergence if ic_state != "validated".
